definition: Enumerate means to list items one by one.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word enumerate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know enumerate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Before naming her price, the realtor enumerated the cottage's failings: the well, the wiring, the chimney, and the stairs, in that order.
Mention touches a thing once in passing — the opposite of an accounting; it stops far short of enumerate.
List goes further than mention but stops short of enumerate, which insists on one-by-one completeness, first item to last.

To itemize is to break a total into its billed parts — the line items on a receipt, an invoice, a tax return. Enumerate is not about money at all: to enumerate is to tell things one by one, first to last, so the whole accounting is out loud and complete.

To tally is to count items toward a total — tick marks on a clipboard where the final number matters more than the naming. Enumerate points the other way: the number is incidental; what counts is naming every item, one by one, no item merged and none left out.

To mention is to touch; to list is to set down; to enumerate is to count the items out loud so everyone can watch the total being built.
Enumerate when the one-by-one telling is the point — grievances, safety checks, the terms of a deal.
